summary: All immutable-release provenance, bootstrap idempotency, dependency detection, and lifecycle-state review findings for issue #71 were fixed and verified.

findings.description: The checked-in manifest claimed a syntactically valid Answer Engine runtime digest without registry evidence, allowing source-checkout installs to treat fabricated metadata as release truth. It is now a non-runnable template; only the exact-commit builder injects and revalidates an explicit registry-inspected digest.
The release workflow wrote runtime-index.json into the checkout immediately before invoking a builder that rejects dirty or untracked checkouts, so every candidate build would fail.
Protected publication used gh release upload --clobber, allowing exact-tag installer assets to be replaced in place despite the immutable download contract.

When bootstrap installed the supported user-scoped Node runtime, it created raw JavaScript symlink launchers that depended on a future shell PATH and therefore failed after bootstrap exited on machines without a system Node installation.
An interrupted bootstrap that had already installed managed Node did not reuse it on rerun and instead refused the existing destination, breaking required bootstrap idempotency.
Compose detection accepted blank or arbitrary successful command output as Compose v2, allowing a required incompatible dependency to pass readiness.
Rerunning a different installer version rewrote ANSWER_ENGINE_IMAGE while preserving the old release-state digest, splitting status and rollback state from the runtime configuration.
Consent and rerun coverage exercised an exported remediation helper that no production bootstrap path called, leaving the real shell dependency flow untested.
